items.title: The Euclidean trace quotient is the fixed-atlas H1/2 boundary space

references.title: Emilio Gagliardo, Caratterizzazioni delle tracce sulla frontiera relative ad alcune classi di funzioni in n variabili (1957)
references.locator: No. 1, Theorem [1.I] and its proof, printed pp. 286–290 (PDF pp. 3–7): trace-space characterization, local boundary norms, and equivalence between the trace norm and quotient norm.

references.title: Maria Kampanou, Trace Theorems for Sobolev Spaces (2018)
references.locator: Chapter 3, Theorems 3.4–3.5 and their proofs, printed pp. 28–31 (PDF pp. 28–31): trace range on a smooth boundary and a bounded extension from the fractional boundary space.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected domain with smooth nonempty boundary, and regard $\overline\Omega$ as a compact smooth manifold with the Euclidean metric. Write $H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)$ be the closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ in that norm; put $\mathcal B_{\rm E}:=H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)/H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)$. Let $H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$ and $H^1_{0,\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$ be the fixed-atlas spaces on $\overline\Omega$ and let $H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega)$ be the fixed-atlas boundary space using localized Euclidean $W^{1/2,2}$ norms. The identity on smooth functions extends to bounded linear isomorphisms between $H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)$ and $H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$, and between their zero-boundary subspaces. Classical boundary restriction extends to a bounded linear trace $T:H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)\to H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega)$ with kernel $H^1_{0,\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$. The induced quotient map is a bounded linear isomorphism

$$H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)/H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)\;\cong\;H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)/H^1_{0,\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)\;\cong\;H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega).$$

Thus the Euclidean trace quotient and the fixed-atlas $H^{1/2}$ boundary space are canonically equivalent.

items.title: Anisotropic conductivity and weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map

references.title: Mikko Salo, The Calderón problem on Riemannian manifolds (2012)
Thierry Daudé, Niky Kamran, and François Nicoleau, A survey of non-uniqueness results for the anisotropic Calderón problem with disjoint data (2018)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected open set with smooth boundary. Write $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $H_0^1(\Omega)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Define the boundary trace-data space $\mathcal B_\Omega:=H^1(\Omega)/H_0^1(\Omega)$ with quotient norm. If $\Omega\ne\varnothing$, its boundary is nonempty, and the trace-quotient lemma identifies this quotient with the fixed-atlas $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data convention of the scalar conductivity map. If $\Omega=\varnothing$, then $H^1(\Omega)=H_0^1(\Omega)=\{0\}$ and the fixed-atlas empty-boundary convention $H^{1/2}(\varnothing)=\{0\}$ gives the identification directly. Let $\gamma\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb R))$ be uniformly positive definite, so some $0<c\le C<\infty$ satisfy $c|\xi|^2\le \xi^T\gamma(x)\xi\le C|\xi|^2$ for all $x\in\overline\Omega$ and $\xi\in\mathbb R^n$. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal B_\Omega$, a weak solution with boundary datum $f$ is a class $u_{\gamma,f}\in H^1(\Omega)$ with $[u_{\gamma,f}]=f$ and

$$\int_\Omega \gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla\varphi\,dx=0\qquad(\varphi\in H_0^1(\Omega)).$$

The weak anisotropic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map is the bilinear-form candidate $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega\to\mathbb R$ given, whenever the weak solution exists, by

$$\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle:=\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla V_h\,dx,$$

where $V_h\in H^1(\Omega)$ is any representative of $h$. The local anisotropic conductivity well-posedness lemma proves existence and uniqueness for every boundary class, independence of the representative $V_h$, and boundedness on $\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega$; it therefore makes this candidate a bounded bilinear map. The map is the boundary energy form for the equation $\operatorname{div}(\gamma\nabla u)=0$. Under the trace-quotient isomorphism and the local boundedness result, this form gives the usual weak map into the dual $H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ with the scalar convention.

items.title: Weak well-posedness of the anisotropic conductivity equation

references.title: Mikko Salo, The Calderón problem on Riemannian manifolds (2012)
Thierry Daudé, Niky Kamran, and François Nicoleau, A survey of non-uniqueness results for the anisotropic Calderón problem with disjoint data (2018)

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected open set with smooth boundary, let $\gamma\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb R))$ satisfy $c|\xi|^2\le\xi^T\gamma(x)\xi\le C|\xi|^2$ for fixed $0<c\le C<\infty$, and let $f\in\mathcal B_\Omega=H^1(\Omega)/H_0^1(\Omega)$ be the boundary trace-data class defined by the anisotropic weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. Then there is a unique $u_{\gamma,f}\in H^1(\Omega)$ with $[u_{\gamma,f}]=f$ and $\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla v\,dx=0$ for every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$. The energy formula defining $\Lambda_\gamma$ is independent of the chosen representative of its second boundary argument and is a bounded bilinear form on $\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega$.

items.title: A boundary-fixing diffeomorphism preserves the anisotropic DN map

references.title: Mikko Salo, The Calderón problem on Riemannian manifolds (2012)
Thierry Daudé, Niky Kamran, and François Nicoleau, A survey of non-uniqueness results for the anisotropic Calderón problem with disjoint data (2018)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, hence Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected domain with smooth boundary, and let $\gamma\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb R))$ be uniformly positive definite. Let $F:\overline\Omega\to\overline\Omega$ be a diffeomorphism smooth through the boundary, with smooth inverse and $F|_{\partial\Omega}=\operatorname{id}$. For $x=F(y)$, put $J_F(y)=|\det DF(y)|$ and define

$$ (F_*\gamma)(x)=\frac{DF(y)\,\gamma(y)\,DF(y)^T}{J_F(y)},\qquad y=F^{-1}(x). $$

Then $F_*\gamma$ is a smooth uniformly positive-definite matrix conductivity and its weak anisotropic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map equals that of $\gamma$. Explicitly, for every pair of boundary trace-data classes $f,h\in\mathcal B_\Omega:=H^1(\Omega)/H_0^1(\Omega)$,

$$\langle\Lambda_{F_*\gamma}f,h\rangle=\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle,$$

where each map is the weak energy form $\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle=\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla V_h\,dx$, $u_{\gamma,f}$ is the unique weak solution with boundary class $f$, and $V_h$ is any $H^1$ representative of $h$.

The same gauge invariance has a Riemannian form. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold with boundary, $g$ a smooth Riemannian metric, $\Gamma\subseteq\partial M$ relatively open, and $\Phi:M\to M$ a smooth diffeomorphism with $\Phi|_\Gamma=\operatorname{id}$. Define $(\Phi^*g)_p(v,w):=g_{\Phi(p)}(D\Phi_pv,D\Phi_pw)$. The cotangent inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_g$ is induced by $g^{-1}$, and in coordinates $dV_g=\sqrt{\det(g_{ij})}|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$. A smooth function $u$ is $g$-harmonic when $\int_M\langle du,d\psi\rangle_g\,dV_g=0$ for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$. Then $u\circ\Phi$ is $\Phi^*g$-harmonic; for any two smooth $g$-harmonic functions $u,v$,

$$\int_M\langle d(u\circ\Phi),d(v\circ\Phi)\rangle_{\Phi^*g}\,dV_{\Phi^*g}=\int_M\langle du,dv\rangle_g\,dV_g.$$

If the boundary traces of $u,v$ are supported in $\Gamma$, then composition by $\Phi$ leaves both traces fixed, so the local energy measurement of every such smooth harmonic pair is unchanged. In particular, if for each $f\in C_c^\infty(\Gamma)$ the Dirichlet solutions for $g$ and $\Phi^*g$ with trace $f$ are unique and smooth, then the corresponding local energy DN maps agree.

items.title: Smooth anisotropic Calderón uniqueness from one boundary patch

references.title: Mikko Salo, The Calderón problem on Riemannian manifolds (2012)
Thierry Daudé, Niky Kamran, and François Nicoleau, A survey of non-uniqueness results for the anisotropic Calderón problem with disjoint data (2018)
OpenAI, Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch (2026-09-24 preprint)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, and let $n\ge3$. Let $M$ be a compact connected smooth $n$-manifold with nonempty smooth boundary and no orientability assumption, and let $\Gamma\subsetneq\partial M$ be a nonempty relatively open patch. Use a fixed finite smooth atlas and subordinate smooth partition of unity. Define $H^1(M)$ as the completion of $C^\infty(M)$ under the sum of localized Euclidean $W^{1,2}$ norms. For each integer $k\ge0$, $H^k(M)$ uses the same completion convention with localized $W^{k,2}$ norms. Let $H_0^1(M)$ be the closure of $C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$ in $H^1(M)$. Define $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ by the same fixed boundary atlas and partition, using localized Euclidean $W^{1/2,2}$ Slobodeckij norms. Let $\operatorname{Tr}:H^1(M)\to H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ be the Sobolev trace, the continuous extension of classical boundary restriction. For a smooth Riemannian metric $g$, write $dV_g=\sqrt{\det(g_{ij})}\,|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$ in coordinates and let $dS_g$ be its induced boundary density; $\langle du,dv\rangle_g$ is the cotangent inner product induced by $g^{-1}$. For $f\in C_c^\infty(\Gamma)$ extended by zero on $\partial M\setminus\Gamma$, let $u_{g,f}\in H^1(M)$ be the unique weak solution with $\operatorname{Tr}u_{g,f}=f$ and

$$\int_M\langle du_{g,f},dv\rangle_g\,dV_g=0\qquad(v\in H_0^1(M)).$$

The zero-boundary kernel is trivial by uniqueness of the positive scalar Dirichlet problem, so the nonresonant elliptic regularity interface applies; for smooth $f$, the solution lies in every integer-order Sobolev space. This is the positive scalar conductivity Dirichlet problem at $\gamma\equiv1$. Define its local zero-frequency energy map, with the same patch for inputs and observations, by

$$\mathcal E_{g,\Gamma}(f,h):=\int_M\langle du_{g,f},du_{g,h}\rangle_g\,dV_g\qquad(f,h\in C_c^\infty(\Gamma)).$$

The displayed energy is the weak scalar DN pairing with the second extension chosen as $u_{g,h}$. If two smooth metrics $g_1,g_2$ on this same manifold satisfy $\mathcal E_{g_1,\Gamma}(f,h)=\mathcal E_{g_2,\Gamma}(f,h)$ for every such pair, must there be a smooth diffeomorphism $\Phi:M\to M$ with $\Phi|_\Gamma=\operatorname{id}$ and $g_2=\Phi^*g_1$, where $(\Phi^*g_1)_p(v,w):=(g_1)_{\Phi(p)}(D\Phi_pv,D\Phi_pw)$?
